title: Church Government: Models and Biblical Form
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Importance of Church Order and Submission
subpoints: Authority and submission are divine attributes
Obedience to church leaders is a biblical mandate
God is a God of order, reflected in creation and worship

outline.title: Models of Church Government in Christendom
subpoints: Episcopacy/Prelacy: Rule by bishops (Catholic, Anglican, Methodist)
Independent Congregationalism: Rule by the local congregation (Baptist, Non-denominational)
Single Pastor Model: Centralized authority in one leader
Presbyterian Model: Rule by plurality of elders and connected courts

outline.title: The Biblical Form of Government
subpoints: Christ is the ultimate head of the church
New Testament authors recognized their subordinate role
Government by presbyters (ministers and ruling elders) is founded on Scripture

outline.title: Constitutional Basis for Presbyterian Government
subpoints: Three ordinary officers: Ministers, Ruling Elders, Deacons
Local church must be 'perfectly formed' with all three offices
Government by presbyters is expedient and agreeable to God's Word

summary:
This lesson continues the series on the city's ecclesiology, focusing specifically on the structure and theology of church government. The teaching emphasizes that authority and submission are fundamental to God's design, citing Hebrews 13:17 to underscore the necessity of obeying church leaders who watch over the souls of the congregation. It argues that understanding the appointed form of government is essential for profitable obedience and spiritual health, reflecting the character of God as an orderly being who created the universe with structure and purpose.

The sermon surveys the primary models of church governance currently practiced in Christendom, including episcopacy (rule by bishops), independent congregationalism (rule by the local body), the single pastor model, and the presbyterian model. It notes that while episcopacy developed post-New Testament, the presbyterian model aligns with the biblical practice of rule by a plurality of elders. The discussion highlights that the presbyterian system, with its connected courts of session, presbytery, and general assembly, provides a structured framework for accountability and order.

Finally, the lesson outlines the specific form of government held by the Bible Presbyterian Church, as defined in its constitution. It affirms that government by presbyters—comprising ministers, ruling elders, and deacons—is founded upon the Word of God. The teaching clarifies that a 'perfectly formed' church is one that possesses all three offices, ensuring that local governance reflects the New Testament pattern and acknowledges Christ as the sole head of the church.
